candidates: Pin all third-party GitHub Actions to an immutable reference — a specific release tag (e.g., `@v1.2.3`) or a full commit SHA — rather than a mutable branch name such as `@master` or `@main`. Mutable refs allow upstream changes to silently alter workflow behavior and are a supply-chain security risk.

Every workflow step that runs `yarn release:publish` (or any command that internally calls `yarn npm publish`) must explicitly declare `YARN_NPM_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}` in its `env:` block. Do not rely solely on job-level `environment:` secret injection to provide npm authentication; omitting the explicit env var will cause the publish command to fail unauthenticated.

Before referencing a step's outputs with `steps.<id>.outputs.<name>`, confirm that a step with that exact `id` is defined within the same job. Referencing an undefined step ID is not a compile-time error in GitHub Actions — it silently evaluates to an empty string, producing incorrect runtime behavior (e.g., wrong flags, wrong environment names).

When constructing a `gh release create` command, pass boolean flags such as `--prerelease` or `--draft` directly on the command line rather than expanding an env variable that holds the string `'false'` as a positional argument. The GitHub CLI treats every positional argument after the tag as an asset file path to upload; passing the string `'false'` will cause the step to fail trying to open a nonexistent file.

When calling a local composite action from a GitHub Actions workflow, the `uses:` directive must point to the directory containing `action.yml` (e.g., `uses: ./.github/actions/my-action`), not to the YAML file itself (e.g., not `uses: ./.github/actions/my-action/action.yml`). GitHub Actions automatically discovers the `action.yml` or `action.yaml` inside the specified directory; including the filename in the path is invalid syntax and will cause the workflow to fail.
